Large language models can exhibit emergent reasoning behaviors, often manifested as recurring lexical patterns (e.g., “wait,” indicating verification). However, complex reasoning trajectories remain sparse in unconstrained sampling, and standard RL often fails to guarantee the acquisition of diverse reasoning behaviors. [research area Knowledge Bases and Search](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/?domain=Knowledge%20Bases%20and%20Search) ,[research area Speech and Natural Language Processing](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/?domain=Speech%20and%20Natural%20Language%20Processing)


Long chain-of-thought (CoT) significantly enhances large language models’ (LLM) reasoning capabilities. However, the extensive reasoning traces lead to inefficiencies and an increased time-to-first-token (TTFT). We propose a novel training paradigm that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to guide reasoning LLMs to interleave thinking and answering for multi-hop questions.
